properties.headline: Heat Advisory issued June 21 at 3:38PM CDT until June 21 at 9:00PM CDT by NWS Lubbock TX
properties.description:
* WHAT...Temperatures up to 106 on the Caprock, and heat indices as
high as 109 off the Caprock.

* WHERE...The South Plains, Rolling Plains, and far southeastern
Texas Panhandle.

* WHEN...Until 9 PM CDT this evening.

* IMPACTS...Hot temperatures may cause heat illnesses.
properties.instruction:
Drink plenty of fluids, stay in an air-conditioned room, stay out of
the sun, and check up on relatives and neighbors.

Take extra precautions when outside. Wear lightweight and loose
fitting clothing. Try to limit strenuous activities to early morning
or evening. Take action when you see symptoms of heat exhaustion and
heat stroke.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued June 21 at 2:39PM CDT until June 26 at 8:00PM CDT by NWS Corpus Christi TX
properties.description:
...Forecast flooding changed from Minor to Moderate severity and
increased in duration for the following rivers in Texas...

Nueces River Near Tilden affecting McMullen County.

For the Nueces River...including Tilden...Moderate flooding is
forecast.

- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 16.0 feet
early Tuesday afternoon. It will then fall below flood stage
early Friday morning.
- Flood stage is 14.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov/crp.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued June 21 at 2:23PM CDT until June 25 at 4:00PM CDT by NWS Houston/Galveston TX
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Texas...

Navasota River near Normangee affecting Brazos, Madison and
Grimes Counties.

For the Navasota River...including Normangee...Moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Navasota River near Normangee.

* WHEN...From Monday morning to Thursday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...At 18.0 feet, Moderate lowland flooding begins as three
channels merge into one below State Highway 21. There is
widespread inundation of the floodplain in the vicinity of the
gage with the river more than 1.5 miles wide. Long Trussel Road in
northeast Brazos County below State Highway 21 becomes inundated.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 2:00 PM CDT Sunday the stage was 10.1 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 12.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise above flood stage
tomorrow morning to a crest of 19.4 feet tomorrow evening. It
will then fall below flood stage early Thursday morning.
- Flood stage is 15.0 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of
19.3 feet on 12/19/2001.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive
cars through flooded areas.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov/hgx.

The next statement will be issued by Monday afternoon at 100 PM CDT.
